reviews.review:
Back 4 Blood takes everything great about cooperative shooters and shines. Every match is a pulse‑pounding battle against hordes of Ridden where teamwork, strategy, and pure chaos collide — and it works in the best possible way.

Gunplay is crisp, satisfying, and packed with weight. Every weapon feels powerful, each reload sounds meaty, and figuring out how to handle different enemy types becomes deeply engaging. Swapping cards and building your deck between runs adds smart strategy to what might otherwise be pure run‑and‑gun action. It’s a brilliant layer that keeps each playthrough feeling fresh and personalized.

What really elevates Back 4 Blood is the way enemies swarm and adapt. Ridden never come in predictable waves — they rush, flank, and surprise you, keeping tension high and teamwork essential. Reviving teammates, coordinating attacks, and watching an intense firefight erupt around you with sound effects that absolutely slam is pure adrenaline.

The pace is phenomenal. Matches feel fast‑moving and urgent, but you’re never overwhelmed if your team communicates and works together. Whether you’re clearing tight corridors or holding a choke point under fire, the dynamic pacing always keeps you engaged.

Visuals and sound are excellent. The environments have character, the gun sounds hit hard, and the audio design makes every collapse, groan, and explosion feel playable and real. Add in fun seasonal content and updates that keep the experience fresh — this game has long‑term replayability written into its DNA.

If you love co‑op shooters that are frantic, rewarding, and genuinely thrilling with a squad — Back 4 Blood delivers in spades.

10/10 — satisfying, chaotic, and endlessly replayable co‑op zombie mayhem.

Decent game to kill time, can be a challenge on higher difficulties. Gunplay is snappy and fluid, movement  is smooth. Card Decks bring something new and fresh to the genre which is nice. They've added the ability to ads and add attachments to weapons which should've been implemented in L4D2 so that's awesome. But here's where the game starts to fall short, and why I believe B4B didn't live up to the success or likeability of L4D. 

1; There's a decent variety of enemies, but none of them are really new... They're just reskins (albeit the visual design of the ridden compared to the infected design of L4D seems goofy, cartoonish, and kinda sucks. They also give me AI design vibes...) 

2; None of the maps in B4B feel unique, and a lot of locations seem like they were ripped straight out of the original 2 games with slight changes and a reskin. I'll say it again, the maps also give me the feeling that they might've been designed by AI.

3; Adding a boss (The Harbinger) was a great idea but poorly executed. The boss presents no challenge whatsoever and feels like it was only thrown into the game for the sake of having a unique boss fight, which doesn't feel like a boss fight at all as it feels more like you're shooting a giant bullet sponge with weak points instead

4; The color pallet mainly consists of blue and red... If you've played Left 4 Dead and L4D2, you'll definitely notice those games had greater color detail and a wider variety of colors that added realism.
I don't know what art style they were going for in B4B but it's not it.

5; Character voice lines are annoying at best. L4D characters were corny at worst, this cast is a bit cringe.

6; Servers need a dedicated player host with the ability to instantly kick unwanted players which would decrease the amount of griefers purposely throwing matches.

All in all, 5/10. Would recommend Left 4 Dead 2 instead, or buy this on a sale.
Would recommend for multiplayer FPS zombie shooting.
Feels like a watered down L4D experience.

People gave this game a lot of grief for not being Left 4 Dead 3, and when they finished support for it and did not release mod tools, they gave it even more grief. The reality is, this game is incredible. The card system was fixed to feel fun and engaging while also making sure your build is online from the start, there is plenty of content, challenges, and things to unlock (especially if you're going after ZWAT skins).

Yes, it's not limitless like Left 4 Dead 2, but it doesn't need to be. The gun play, level design, mutators, character abilities, and pacing all feel great.

Left 4 Dead 2 will forever be legendary, but if you want better gun play and movement, some new and unique mechanics, and more of that style, this is the place to be. It usually goes on sale for dirt cheap and is easily worth the like $10 for the ultimate edition, as the DLCs are fantastic.
